When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. ground_truth.answer: Four dishes have problems: (1) Beef croquetas — croquetas are breaded and fried with flour, which contains gluten; Marcus has celiac disease and cannot eat gluten. (2) Gambas al ajillo (garlic shrimp) — contains shrimp; the user is allergic to shrimp. (3) Tuna tartare — tartare is raw fish; Danielle is pregnant and must avoid raw fish. (4) Romesco dip with bread — traditional romesco sauce contains almonds (tree nuts); Danielle has a severe tree nut allergy. Additionally, the bread served with romesco contains gluten, problematic for Marcus. Patatas bravas is fine for everyone. Manchego and quince plate is fine — manchego is a pasteurized aged cheese, safe for pregnancy, and quince paste has no constraint issues.
required_elements: Beef croquetas are problematic for Marcus: croquetas are breaded/battered with flour which contains gluten, and Marcus has celiac disease
Gambas al ajillo is problematic for the user: it is garlic shrimp, and the user is allergic to shrimp
Tuna tartare is problematic for Danielle: tartare is raw fish, and Danielle is pregnant so she must avoid raw fish
Romesco dip is problematic for Danielle: traditional romesco contains almonds which are tree nuts, and Danielle has a severe tree nut allergy
Patatas bravas is fine for everyone currently attending
Manchego and quince plate is fine — manchego is pasteurized aged cheese, safe for Danielle's pregnancy
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish for Jain/vegetarian reasons (Priya cancelled and is no longer attending)
Flagging patatas bravas as problematic for anyone (potatoes are fine for all current diners — Priya who avoids root vegetables is gone)
Saying the user has a general seafood allergy (user specifically reacted to shrimp, not all seafood)
Flagging manchego as unsafe for pregnancy (manchego is a pasteurized hard cheese, safe for pregnant women)
Saying Marcus cannot eat beef croquetas because of the beef (the issue is the gluten in the breading, not the beef itself)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 turns. The agent must track: (1) Marcus has celiac disease → no gluten → breaded croquetas are out (inferential chain from diagnosis to ingredient). (2) Priya is Jain → strict vegetarian + no root vegetables, BUT she cancels — her constraints must be REMOVED. (3) The user has a shrimp allergy (direct). (4) Danielle JOINS LATE (turn 6) with TWO constraints: pregnancy → no raw fish/meat, no unpasteurized cheese; and tree nut allergy → no almonds/walnuts/etc. (5) Romesco sauce traditionally contains almonds — this is a hidden ingredient inference (romesco → almonds → tree nuts → Danielle's allergy). At probe time, the over-generalization trap is: user had a shrimp reaction ≠ all seafood allergy (tuna tartare is NOT flagged for the user). The removed-entity trap is: Priya left, so patatas bravas (potato = root vegetable) is now fine. The late-joiner test is: Danielle's pregnancy and nut allergy must both be applied to tuna tartare and romesco respectively.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
